# Two balls that cover a ball, two-limb center

Kernel `ball_split_2` · **UNVERIFIED** · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

**UNVERIFIED: no proof is checked.** The statement below is a target: Rocq has not checked a proof of it. No public operation calls it yet ([What holds today](../getting-started/guarantees.md#proved-and-unverified)).

## What it computes

Two balls that together cover the ball $X$ of center $c$ and radius $r$, one each half:

$$[c - r, c] \subseteq [c_a - r_a, c_a + r_a], \qquad [c, c + r] \subseteq [c_b - r_b, c_b + r_b].$$

A number of several limbs stands for their exact sum: $c = c_0 + c_1$, $c_a = c_{a0} + c_{a1}$, $c_b = c_{b0} + c_{b1}$.

## C++

**Not yet called by the public headers.** No public operation computes this kernel yet.

## Requires

- the ball of center $c$ and radius $r$ is a canonical ball: a finite ball (finite center, normalized, finite radius $\ge 0$), the whole line (center 0, radius $+\infty$), or the empty set (every limb a NaN).

## Target (not proved)

For operands that satisfy the requirements, finite, infinite or NaN:

- The two parts, of centers $c_a$ and $c_b$ and radii $r_a$ and $r_b$, are canonical balls.
- If the ball $X$ of center $c$ and radius $r$ is empty, both parts are; if it is the whole line, both are the whole line.
- Otherwise every real number of $[c - r, c]$ is a member of the first part, and every one of $[c, c + r]$ a member of the second.
- Not claimed: that the parts are inside $X$, nor that their radii are close to $r/2$.

Stated for every binary format with a precision of at least 3 bits, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the IEEE model, with signed zeros, infinities, NaN and overflow. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**UNVERIFIED.** No proof of the statement is checked. The [Proofs](../proofs/index.md#what-is-proved-and-in-which-model) page says which statements of the IEEE model are proved against statements written by hand; this page gives the status that `gen/claims.json` gives.

## Source

**Algorithm:** the point c plus the balls (-h, q) and (h, q), q = max(h, r - h), by the proved ball sum of two limbs (Milestone 2 listing). **License:** algorithm and proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/ball_split_2.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/ball_split_2.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal model (`proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).
It calls [`make_2`](make_2.md), [`ball_add_2_full`](ball_add_2_full.md).

```
# Two balls that together cover a ball with a 2-limb center (milestone2.md, "One enclosure
# interface", "Hull, intersection and split of balls"): ball_split_1 on the sum of two limbs, the
# point c plus the balls of center -h and +h (the 2-limb numbers (-h, 0) and (h, 0), by make_2, so
# that no limb is added to a literal zero) and radius q = max(h, r - h), h = RN(r/2), by
# ball_add_2_full. The first contains [c - r, c], the second [c, c + r]; the whole line and the
# empty set are returned twice, as they are. -h is its own product of the negated radius, as in
# ball_split_1 (no fused result negated).

h             = prod(r, const up(1/2))
nr            = neg(r)
hn            = prod(nr, const up(1/2))
g             = sub(r, h)
mg            = lt(h, g)
q             = select(mg, g, h)
fr            = lt(r, const inf)
hs            = select(fr, h, 0)
nh            = select(fr, hn, 0)
ws            = select(fr, q, 0)
cs0           = select(fr, c0, 0)
cs1           = select(fr, c1, 0)
(n0, n1)      = make_2(nh)
(p0, p1)      = make_2(hs)
(a0, a1, ar)  = ball_add_2_full(cs0, cs1, 0, n0, n1, ws)
(b0, b1, br)  = ball_add_2_full(cs0, cs1, 0, p0, p1, ws)
ca0           = select(fr, a0, c0)
ca1           = select(fr, a1, c1)
ra            = select(fr, ar, r)
cb0           = select(fr, b0, c0)
cb1           = select(fr, b1, c1)
rb            = select(fr, br, r)
```
